status: Post-hoc descriptive analysis of previously inspected input-stage pilots; not a preregistered hypothesis test
grouping: Primary: three groups by average E rank within the 566 non-basis tokens of each image. Rank <= n/3 is low, <= 2n/3 is middle, otherwise high. Equal E values are never split. FPS basis sources are a separate group. Secondary: repeat with four rank groups as a bin-boundary sensitivity check.
score: Primary signed I = S(full) - S(single projected embedding zeroed), in mean reference-answer nats/token. Absolute I is explicitly auxiliary. Group means/medians describe separate singleton effects; neither sums nor means are joint interventions.
aggregation: Compute groups and high-minus-low contrasts within each question; summarize question contrasts within dataset. Also average question contrasts per image and report the median over images. No pooled-token p-values or population/dataset-difference claims.
pairs: GQA same-image pairs require exact matching CLIP/projected feature hashes, seed, all E values and native roles. Compare signed-I Spearman and overlap of the 57 highest signed-I non-basis patches. Top-set ties use patch index; log their boundary count. Sign disagreement uses both effects exceeding 0.0001 nats/token in magnitude, a descriptive cutoff rather than a measured noise floor.
mmstar_sensitivity: Additionally summarize without previously flagged cases 604 (two real choices) and 617 (option-name typo), without discarding their saved measurements.

limitations: Examples are explicitly selected after observing saved E/I; qualitative illustrations are not independent confirmation.
Question wording, fixed answer, answer-token length and reference confidence vary within GQA pairs.
A missing directly retained original feature may still contribute through native basis replacement or merging.
Contextualized CLIP features and artificial zeroing prevent literal pixel-relevance claims, including on padding.
Calibration and MMStar3 repeats are excluded from canonical counts; no GPU inference is performed.
